Odin × Godot

Character movement, queries and joints

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Tick ownership and character stateDeterministic queriesCalling from each frameworkJoint families and identityComplete recovery and limitsRequired validation

P5.2 extends the shared authoring backend through separate Kit and Replay execution adapters. The Native matrix, pure and Native-facing Odin tests, both framework transaction and canonical-transfer cases, and actual Godot SDK fixture pass on the declared macOS reference. Exact artifacts and limits are in the task report.

Tick ownership and character state#

Box3DCharacterMover3D authors a capsule and its movement settings. It does not schedule physics. Extract its configuration before simulation and store the character position, velocity and grounded state in rollback-owned Game or Side. Kit and Replay call the shared mover from their existing staged tick callbacks. Presentation reads the published value and updates nodes afterward.

Movement uses the pinned engine's capsule cast, collision-plane collection, plane solver and velocity clipping. Query filters and an explicit body exclusion apply to the same actual execution world. No Godot query, Resource lookup, process clock or live node reference participates in replay. Floor classification uses a declared up vector and slope threshold. An unsupported or exhausted query returns an error instead of publishing movement based on a partial set.

Deterministic queries#

The original raw AABB and ray queries retain their documented traversal order. The new deterministic operations gather the complete bounded result, convert handles to world-independent allocation keys, and apply stable ordering and tie breaks before copying to the caller. Capacity is explicit. Stable allocation keys are valid within the recorded world history; they do not replace durable authored logical IDs across unrelated construction histories.

Framework helpers query the unpublished staged solver. Callers copy results into their own value state; they never retain the borrowed execution world. Rejected ticks, actions and commit gates preserve both character side-state and the complete solver through the frameworks' existing transaction machinery.

Calling from each framework#

The shared runtime types are Character_Config, Character_State and Character_Result in godot:box3d. Build-time character maps supply a copied configuration and initial state. A mover does not create a hidden dynamic body; its optional self-exclusion resolves an authored body reference to a local allocation key during construction.

Inside a Kit authored tick, use the current Side and the staged helper:

Odin
side := kp.state(physics)
next, error := kp.character_step(physics, movement_config, side.character)
if error != .Ok {return}
side.character = next.state

Inside Replay's existing step callback:

Odin
next, error := rp.character_step(ctx.execution, movement_config, game.character)
if error != .None {return}
game.character = next.state
if rp.step(ctx.execution) != .None {return}

The callback supplies desired velocity in its rollback-owned state, including any game-specific gravity or jump rule. Both adapter movement helpers use the existing fixed 1/60 step. Kit still performs its participant solver step; Replay still requires exactly one ordinary rp.step. The mover itself only reads the world and returns a candidate value. Invalid movement poisons the unpublished transaction even if its error is ignored.

Both adapters expose motion_aabb, motion_ray, motion_capsule and motion_capsule_cast with copied Motion_Hit results and a Motion_Filter. They expose motion_joint_create and motion_joint_destroy for staged commands using body/joint allocation keys. Replay dispatches mutations through the producer that owns the execution and its accounting. Read results only after checking status. Capacity from a read query remains an explicit sizing result; no partial prefix is published by the deterministic query API.

Joint families and identity#

The named authoring surfaces map to the pinned engine as follows:

Authoring kind Native constraint
Pin Spherical point constraint with angular features disabled
Hinge Revolute
Slider Prismatic
Spherical Spherical with its explicit angular settings
Distance Distance
Motor Motor
Weld Weld
Wheel Wheel

Joint definitions reference explicit body keys in the same authored world. Their own stable keys produce durable logical IDs independent of node names, resource order and runtime handles. Baking validates references, rigid local frames, finite settings and limit relationships before native construction. The local runtime map contains native joint allocation keys for executing later operations. Neither Godot object identities nor native handles enter canonical Game state.

Complete recovery and limits#

Schema 1 keeps its earlier body/shape content identity and recovery format 2. Use scene_input_default(namespace, 2) for joint/character arrays. Schema 2 uses the same copied asset descriptor layout with a recovery-format-3 catalog. Legacy primitive format 1 and authored format 2 retain their earlier readers. The new format carries every supported native joint union; no solver field is omitted. The wrapper normalizes default Distance length bounds through the engine's setter before publishing the key, including a disabled 0..0 range. Inverted native ranges remain invalid canonical data.

A locally created constraint is usable in networked rollback only after the canonical codec covers its complete solver state. Every joint family requires its actual settings, impulses, prepared solver data and native graph links to survive validation, scratch reconstruction and exact re-encoding. Unsupported format versions fail explicitly; legacy recovery readers keep their declared contracts. No joint family may be silently omitted from a checkpoint.

The existing profile still permits one joint at a time, 35 bodies/shapes, 32 dynamic bodies, eight deduplicated geometry assets, H128 and prediction and ordinary repair depth eight. Tests exercise joint families separately under that profile. Adding authoring classes does not increase the 64 MiB tracked resource limit or change the dependency pin and floating-point policy.

Required validation#

The task must establish Native Debug, Release and sanitizer coverage; pure schema/identity/reference controls; actual native Odin construction and movement; Kit and Replay rollback, rejected-publication and canonical recovery checks; and ordinary Godot import plus Resource/scene save/reload, source destruction and checked cleanup. Editor gizmos and export Gate C are separate tasks.
